'''Erik Peter Verlinde''' ({{IPA|nl|ˈeːrɪk ˈpeːtər vərˈlɪndə|lang}}; born 21 January 1962) is a Dutch [[theoretical physics|theoretical physicist]] and [[string theory|string theorist]]. He is the [[identical twin]] brother of physicist [[Herman Verlinde]]. The [[Verlinde formula]], which is important in [[conformal field theory]] and [[topological field theory]], is named after him. His research deals with string theory, [[gravity]],<ref name="BT-2190814" /> [[black hole]]s and [[physical cosmology|cosmology]]. Currently,<ref>{{cite web|url=http://iop.uva.nl/profile/v/e/e.p.verlinde/e.p.verlinde.html?origin=btqEAcsOSoanWfBtRR4amQ|title=University of Amsterdam homepage|date=14 January 2020}}</ref> he works at the Institute for Theoretical Physics at the [[University of Amsterdam]].

At a symposium at the Dutch Spinoza-institute on 8 December 2009 he introduced a theory of [[entropic gravity]]. In this theory, [[gravity]] exists because of a difference in concentration of information in the empty space between two masses and its surroundings; he also extrapolates this to [[general relativity]] and [[quantum mechanics]]. He said in an interview with the newspaper ''[[de Volkskrant]]'',<ref>{{cite web|url=http://staff.science.uva.nl/~erikv/page15/page13/page13.html|title=De Volkskrant 27 January 2010|language=nl|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131111174823/http://staff.science.uva.nl/~erikv/page15/page13/page13.html|archive-date=11 November 2013|url-status=dead|access-date=11 September 2011}}</ref> "On the smallest level [[Newton's laws]] don't apply, but they do for [[Isaac Newton#Apple incident|apple]]s and [[planet]]s. You can compare this to the pressure of a gas. [[Molecule]]s themselves don't have any pressure, but a barrel of gas has." It appears that Verlinde's approach to explaining gravity leads naturally to the correct observed strength of [[dark energy]].<ref>{{cite web|last=Koelman|first=Johannes|title=It from bit: how to get rid of dark energy|url=http://www.scientificblogging.com/hammock_physicist/it_bit_how_get_rid_dark_energy|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100119223903/http://www.scientificblogging.com/hammock_physicist/it_bit_how_get_rid_dark_energy|url-status=dead|archive-date=19 January 2010|access-date=20 August 2011}}</ref>

==Biography==
Erik Verlinde was born in the Dutch village of [[Woudenberg]] on 21 January 1962, together with his identical twin brother, [[Herman Verlinde]].<ref name="CV">{{cite web|url=http://staff.science.uva.nl/~erikv/page17/page17.html|title=Curriculum Vitae|last=Verlinde|first=Erik|website=Website of Erik Verlinde|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140714122051/http://staff.science.uva.nl/~erikv/page17/page17.html|archive-date=14 July 2014|url-status=dead}}
</ref> He went to school in the nearby city of [[Utrecht]], where he graduated from the [[gymnasium (school)|gymnasium]] in 1980.

That fall he began his studies in theoretical physics together with his brother at [[Utrecht University]]. There he studied with his brother Herman, [[Robbert Dijkgraaf]], and [[Kareljan Schoutens]]. He wrote his Master's thesis with Nobel laureate [[Gerard 't Hooft]].<ref name="CV"/>

In 1985, Verlinde started work on his PhD at Utrecht University under the formal supervision of [[Bernard de Wit]]. He worked again with Herman and Dijkgraaf, and in practice the trio supervised themselves. The original arrangement was that only one of them would be working on the emerging field of [[string theory]], but in the end all three of them wrote their theses on the subject. In September 1988 Erik defended his PhD thesis, which included the [[Verlinde formula]].<ref name="CV"/><ref name="NWO">{{cite web
|url=http://www.nwo.nl/onderzoek-en-resultaten/programmas/spinozapremie/spinozalaureaten/alfabetisch+overzicht+spinozalaureaten/erik+verlinde
|title=Erik Verlinde
|publisher=NWO
|access-date=17 June 2014
|archive-date=14 July 2014
|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140714182051/http://www.nwo.nl/onderzoek-en-resultaten/programmas/spinozapremie/spinozalaureaten/alfabetisch+overzicht+spinozalaureaten/erik+verlinde
|url-status=dead
}}</ref><ref name="QU">{{cite web
|
url=http://www.quantumuniverse.nl/biografie-erik-verlinde
|

|
publisher=Quantum Universe

access-date=17 June 2014

|
url-status=dead
}}</ref>

After his PhD, Verlinde joined the [[Institute for Advanced Study]] in Princeton as a postdoctoral fellow. In 1993, he was added to the permanent staff of the theory division of [[CERN]] in Geneva. At the age of 34 he was appointed full professor of theoretical physics at Utrecht University. Only a few years later, in 1999, he left for [[Princeton University]] to take up a professorial position there. In 2003, he returned to the Netherlands to become a professor in the string theory group led by Robbert Dijkgraaf at the [[University of Amsterdam]].<ref name="CV"/><ref name="NWO"/><ref name="QU"/>

==Major contributions==
Verlinde's main field of research is [[string theory]]. Over the years, he has introduced a number of results that have become important in the development of the theory, and in the study of [[pure mathematics]].

===Verlinde formula===
{{main article|Verlinde formula}}
Verlinde's PhD thesis was titled "Conformal Field Theory Applied to Strings". In it he investigated [[conformal field theory|conformal field theories]] in two dimensions and their relation to the description of the [[world sheet]] of fundamental strings. As part of the project he extended fusion or [[Verlinde algebra]]s, describing conformal field theories with a finite number of fields.<ref>{{cite journal
|title=Fusion Rules and Modular Transformations in 2D Conformal Field Theory
|first=Erik
|last=Verlinde
|journal=Nucl. Phys. B
|volume=300
|year=1988
|doi=10.1016/0550-3213(88)90603-7|bibcode = 1988NuPhB.300..360V
|pages=360–376}}</ref> A main result was an explicit formula for the [[fusion rules]] of these algebras, now known as the Verlinde formula. This has proven to be a highly non-trivial mathematical result. In Verlinde's original work, the formula followed from mainly physical arguments, but since its introduction many formal mathematical proofs have been provided.<ref>{{cite book
|title=A Mathematical Introduction to Conformal Field Theory
|first=Martin
|last=Schottenloher
|publisher=Springer
|year=2008
|isbn=9783540686255|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=PkEqFYpQNggC&pg=PA213
}}</ref>

=== Cardy formula extensions ===
{{main article|Cardy formula}}
The [[Cardy formula]] is an important result in conformal field theory that allows the calculation of the entropy of a 1+1 dimensional conformal field theory. Using the [[AdS/CFT correspondence]] between conformal field theories and quantum gravity in [[AdS|anti-de Sitter spaces]] with one additional dimension, it can be used to calculate (the quantum corrections to) the entropy of [[BTZ black hole|black holes in 2+1 dimensions]]. In 2000, Verlinde extended Cardy's result to conformal field theories of arbitrary dimension,<ref>{{cite arXiv
| last=Erik
| first=Verlinde
| title=On the Holographic Principle in a Radiation Dominated Universe
| year=2000 |eprint= hep-th/0008140 }}</ref>{{primary source inline|date=March 2018}}
allowing the calculation of entropy of black holes in any dimension.

===Entropic gravity===
{{main article|Entropic gravity}}
In 2009, Verlinde showed that the laws of gravity may be derived by assuming a form of the [[holographic principle]] and the [[laws of thermodynamics]].<ref name="entropicgravity">{{cite journal |author=E.P. Verlinde |doi=10.1007/JHEP04(2011)029 |journal=JHEP |volume=2011 |issue=4 |article-number=29 |title=On the Origin of Gravity and the Laws of Newton |year=2011 |bibcode = 2011JHEP...04..029V |arxiv = 1001.0785 |s2cid=3597565 }}</ref> This may imply that gravity is not a true fundamental force of nature (like e.g. [[electromagnetism]]), but instead is a consequence of the universe striving to maximize entropy.

===Emergent gravity and the dark universe===
On 8 November 2016 Erik Verlinde published his new theory of gravity, where gravity is not one of the four fundamental forces of physics but, rather, gravity is [[emergence|emergent]] from other fundamental forces.<ref name="BT-2190814">{{cite news |last=Ratner |first=Paul |title=Physicist advances a radical theory of gravity - Erik Verlinde has been compared to Einstein for completely rethinking the nature of gravity. |url=https://bigthink.com/surprising-science/physicist-radical-theory-of-gravity |date=14 August 2019 |work=[[Big Think]] |access-date=15 August 2019 }}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.quantamagazine.org/erik-verlindes-gravity-minus-dark-matter-20161129/|title=Erik Verlinde's Gravity Minus Dark Matter|first=Natalie|last=Wolchover|magazine=[[Quanta Magazine]]|date=November 29, 2016|access-date=2018-11-20}}</ref><ref>[http://www.uva.nl/en/news-events/news/uva-news/content/press-releases/2016/11/new-theory-of-gravity-might-explain-dark-matter.html New theory of gravity might explain dark matter, E. P. Verlinde, 2016 Nov 8] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161111083805/http://www.uva.nl/en/news-events/news/uva-news/content/press-releases/2016/11/new-theory-of-gravity-might-explain-dark-matter.html |date=11 November 2016 }}</ref> In this work, he argues that unlike in anti-de Sitter (AdS) space, holography and the area law do not apply exactly in de Sitter space (which models our universe) because there is an additional entropy associated with the [[cosmological horizon]]. If this entropy were evenly distributed throughout space, it would contribute a volume law term to the entropy which becomes dominant at large length scales and is related to dark energy. He further argues that this entropy modifies emergent gravity, introducing residual forces when the acceleration due to gravity is very weak.<ref>Erik P. Verlinde, ''Emergent Gravity and the Dark Universe'', SciPost Phys. '''2''', 016 (2017)[https://scipost.org/SciPostPhys.2.3.016]</ref> The result provides a candidate explanation for dark matter similar to the [[Modified Newtonian Dynamics]] (MOND) proposal and explains the empirical relationship between dark matter and the [[Hubble constant]]. By 1 August 2018 the paper has been quoted in 153 physics papers, including by well-known physicists such as [[Lee Smolin]], and [[Mordehai Milgrom]] - originator of MOND. Explanation of modified gravity through entropic gravity is a "quantum gravity theory" merging "general theory of relativity" with "quantum field theory". Verlinde himself names it also quantum information theory. 

There are already critical papers on "emergent gravity" such as "Inconsistencies in Verlinde's emergent gravity"<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Dai |first1=De-Chang |last2=Stojkovic |first2=Dejan |date=November 2017 |title=Inconsistencies in Verlinde's emergent gravity |journal=Journal of High Energy Physics |volume=2017 |issue=11 |pages=7 |doi=10.1007/JHEP11(2017)007 |issn=1029-8479|doi-access=free |arxiv=1710.00946 |bibcode=2017JHEP...11..007D }}</ref> by D Dai, D Stojkovic (Springer HEP, Nov 2017), stating that "...When properly done, Verlinde's
elaborate procedure recovers the standard Newtonian gravity instead of MOND".

==Awards and honors==
In June 2011, the Netherlands Organisation for Scientific Research (NWO) awarded Verlinde the [[Spinoza Prize]], the highest award available to Dutch scientists including a 2.5 million euro grant for future research.<ref>{{cite web |title=NWO-Spinoza Laureates 2011 |url=http://www.nwo.nl/nwohome.nsf/pages/NWOP_5VNCW6_Eng |access-date=20 August 2011 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110822072703/http://www.nwo.nl/nwohome.nsf/pages/NWOP_5VNCW6_Eng |archive-date=22 August 2011 |df=dmy }}</ref> The committee cited his work on the Verlinde formula, the [[Witten–Dijkgraaf–Verlinde–Verlinde equations]], the Cardy-Verlinde formula and entropic gravity as the major achievements leading to the award.
